insanityTips: Treat Spirit as a “rule-out” ghost: confirm what it is NOT (no special hunt traits, no unique abilities).
If you have incense, the long post-smudge cooldown is still your best confirmation even with 1 evidence.
If the ghost feels ordinary acrosss hunts/events and nothing else lines up, Spirit is a strong final call.
name: Spirit
nightmareTips: Use incense (smudge) timing: Spirit is blocked from hunting for ~180s (roughly double the usual).
If you can safely force/observe two hunts, the longer post-smudge cooldown is the main behavioural tell.
If everything else fits but there are no unique tells showing up, Spirit often becomes your “default” after ruling others out.
summary: A baseline ghost type with no extreme behaviour. Use smudge tests and elimination when evidence overlaps.

insanityTips: Salt + UV is still one of the cleanest low-evidence checks: no UV footprints after stepping through salt strongly points to Wraith.
Keep an eye on interactions far from the ghost room; Wraith can make the investigation feel “spread out”.
If you can’t get a hunt tell, rely on salt behaviour and unusual movement/interaction patterns.
name: Wraith
nightmareTips: Salt test: Wraith will not leave UV footprints from salt (no footprint trails).
Watch for sudden “teleport-like” interactions near players (it can move to players and interact away from the room).
If you hear steps but never see footprint UV from salt, keep Wraith high on the list.
summary: Known for mobility and avoiding salt. Pay attention to footsteps and UV behaviour when testing.

insanityTips: Use the hunt blink rate: Phantom is often harder to track visually because it stays invisible longer.
A successful ghost photo causing an instant vanish is a strong behavioural confirmation.
If you’re stuck between Phantom and other DOTS/Spirit Box ghosts, hunt visibility is usually the decider.
name: Phantom
nightmareTips: Photo test: taking a ghost photo causes a Phantom to vanish briefly (events end fast).
During hunts it tends to blink less often (longer invisible periods) compared to many ghosts.
If DOTS is present, try taking a photo when it walks through DOTS: Phantom will not show in the photo.
summary: Often tricky in photos. Use consistent checks and watch for interaction patterns.

insanityTips: Set up a throw pile and listen: a burst of rapid throws is your best low-evidence confirmation.
If you’re getting constant object throws while other evidence refuses to appear, Poltergeist stays likely.
Keep sanity in mind: frequent throws can chip sanity fast, so don’t overstay while testing.
name: Poltergeist
nightmareTips: Watch for multi-throws: Poltergeist can throw several items almost at once.
Pile small objects in the ghost room; a “polty bomb” throw is a big giveaway.
Heavy item chaos early (lots of throws, lots of noise) usually isn’t subtle.
summary: A throw-heavy ghost. Cluttered rooms become dangerous during hunts and events.

insanityTips: If you have parabolic access, the Banshee scream remains one of the cleanest Insanity IDs.
Solo play removes the target gimmick, so rely more on parabolic and hunt behaviour than “target” feelings.
If it feels selective in multiplayer (one person gets punished), keep Banshee high.
name: Banshee
nightmareTips: In multiplayer, it can “pick a target” and behave oddly around non-target players.
Use the parabolic mic: Banshee has a unique scream that can identify it.
If one player is repeatedly pressured while others feel safe, suspect Banshee.
summary: Target-focused behaviour can show up in multiplayer. Track the target and activity over time.

insanityTips: Force a comparison: observe hunt speed with breaker ON vs OFF (Jinn loses its main advantage when power is off).
If you’re getting “fast LoS speed” without cold-speed behaviour (Hantu), Jinn becomes a strong pick.
Use safer tests: keep a known hiding route and don’t intentionally feed long LoS unless you’re ready.
name: Jinn
nightmareTips: Breaker on test: with the power on, Jinn can move faster when it has line-of-sight during hunts.
It cannot turn the breaker off directly; if the breaker stays on consistently, Jinn is more plausible.
If hunts feel unusually fast only when the breaker is on, that’s your strongest tell.
summary: Power-dependent behaviour. Fuse box and line-of-sight decisions matter.

insanityTips: On Insanity, treat Mare as a “lighting pattern” ghost: test with room lights ON vs OFF and compare activity.
If hunts/events happen more in darkness and calm down in light, Mare stays high.
If you can’t prove a special hunt trait, consistent light preference is your best evidence.
name: Mare
nightmareTips: Light behaviour: Mare prefers darkness and can be more aggressive when lights are off.
If lights keep getting switched off quickly after you turn them on, that pattern can point toward Mare.
Try keeping the ghost room lit; if activity drops noticeably in light, Mare is more likely.
summary: Light-sensitive behaviour. Manage lighting deliberately and watch for room changes.

insanityTips: Use a safe speed test: get it to see you briefly, then break LoS and listen for the immediate slowdown.
If it stays fast even without seeing you, it’s probably not a Revenant.
This is one of the most reliable 1-evidence IDs because the speed difference is so extreme.
name: Revenant
nightmareTips: Hunt speed tell: Revenant is extremely fast when it detects a player, but slow when it does not.
Break line of sight and listen: the speed change is dramatic and very readable.
If it feels “unescapeable” when seen but manageable when hidden, Revenant is a prime suspect.
summary: Movement speed is the big tell. Use safe loops and plan smudge timing.

insanityTips: On Insanity, treat Shade as a behaviour pattern: “nothing happens when I’m there, things happen when I’m gone.”
If you get very little activity and a late hunt, Shade stays in the running.
If it is constantly active around players, it’s probably not a Shade.
name: Shade
nightmareTips: Shade is shy: less likely to do interactions/events when players are in the ghost room.
If you only get activity after leaving the room (or watching from a distance), Shade becomes more likely.
Camera/van watching can be more productive than provoking it directly.
summary: Prefers solitude. Evidence can be slower if the room is crowded.

insanityTips: On Insanity, an unusually early hunt is often your biggest Demon clue—prioritise safety and crucifix placement.
If you can control it, compare hunt timing with other candidates; Demon tends to pressure you earlier.
If everything feels “too soon, too fast” and nothing else fits, don’t ignore Demon.
name: Demon
nightmareTips: Early hunt risk: Demon can hunt much earlier than most ghosts.
Crucifix range is more effective against Demon; place one early if you suspect it.
If you get aggressive behaviour very early with little setup time, Demon is a serious candidate.
summary: Aggressive behaviour and early hunts are common tells. Stay disciplined with sanity and crucifixes.

insanityTips: On Insanity, sanity drain + door behaviour becomes your main Yurei evidence.
If doors in/near the ghost room keep moving aggressively and sanity drops feel harsher than normal, keep Yurei high.
If you can’t get a hunt tell, track door patterns and sanity change over time.
name: Yurei
nightmareTips: Door behaviour: watch for strong door interactions (including fully closing doors) around the ghost room.
Yurei can heavily drain sanity with its ability—if sanity dips hard without obvious causes, suspect it.
Incense in the ghost room can “trap” it temporarily, making activity patterns easier to read.
summary: Sanity pressure can feel stronger. Use room control and watch for door behaviour.

insanityTips: If the ghost is constantly eventing and feels “loud”, Oni becomes more likely.
Use event types: repeated full manifestations (and no airball) help narrow toward Oni.
If activity is consistently low and shy, it’s probably not an Oni.
name: Oni
nightmareTips: Oni is very active and tends to show itself more (more frequent ghost events).
It cannot do the “airball” mist ghost event; lots of full-form events points toward Oni.
DOTS is easier to witness in person than from the van (Oni is more active when you’re nearby).
summary: Very active and visible. Strong on events — use them for identification.

insanityTips: On Insanity, use a controlled “voice test”: talk near the ghost room and see if aggression spikes.
In hunts, stay quiet and compare its tracking; Yokai often feels dumber at range.
If it consistently tracks you through walls/at long range, it’s probably not Yokai.
name: Yokai
nightmareTips: Talking near the ghost can make it more aggressive—test by speaking near the room and watch response.
During hunts, Yokai has shorter detection range for electronics/voices than many ghosts.
If it struggles to find you while you’re quiet (even with electronics nearby), Yokai is plausible.
summary: Audio can influence it. Be careful with voice and electronics when testing.

insanityTips: On Insanity, use “cold speed” as your main confirmation: compare speed in cold corridors vs warmer areas.
If turning the breaker ON noticeably weakens its speed profile over time, Hantu becomes more likely.
If it’s fast but not temperature-linked, look at Jinn/Raiju/Moroi instead.
name: Hantu
nightmareTips: Temperature speed tell: Hantu is faster in colder areas and slower in warmer areas.
With the breaker OFF, rooms cool down more—if hunts speed up over time as the building chills, suspect Hantu.
It can show visible cold breath in hunts when the breaker is off and the area is cold.
summary: Cold-related behaviour. Track temps and use the breaker strategy.

insanityTips: On Insanity, treat Goryo as “camera DOTS + low roaming”: set cameras and check from safety.
If the ghost keeps interacting in the same room for a long time, Goryo becomes more likely.
If you’re seeing DOTS in person frequently, it’s probably not a Goryo.
name: Goryo
nightmareTips: DOTS camera test: Goryo DOTS is much easier (or only) to see through a video camera rather than in person.
It tends not to roam far; if the ghost stays very “room-locked”, that supports Goryo.
If DOTS refuses to show in person but appears on camera, keep Goryo high.
summary: Often best confirmed via camera. Approach DOTS checks methodically.

insanityTips: On Insanity, do a safe sound test in a hunt: if it “appears silently” until close, Myling is a strong call.
If you can clearly hear footsteps from far away during hunts, it’s probably not a Myling.
Use parabolic readings + hunt sound behaviour together for higher confidence.
name: Myling
nightmareTips: During hunts, you may hear footsteps only when it’s very close—Myling is quieter than most.
Use the flashlight blink vs footsteps: if lights blink but you don’t hear steps until it’s near, suspect Myling.
Parabolic mic can help because Myling tends to be more audible through it outside hunts.
summary: Sound tells matter. Compare footsteps to hunting range and audio cues.

insanityTips: On Insanity, candles are both defence and evidence: repeated blowouts tied to hunts is your best Onryo tell.
If hunts happen without a pattern around flames, it might be another ghost.
If you can control the environment, the “candle first” behaviour is very readable.
name: Onryo
nightmareTips: Candle test: Onryo treats flames like a crucifix—candles can prevent hunts until they’re blown out.
If it repeatedly blows out candles and then hunts soon after, Onryo becomes very likely.
Try a cluster: candles + crucifix setup to see if candle blowouts line up with hunt attempts.
summary: Fire and candles interact with its behaviour. Use candle tests carefully.

insanityTips: On Insanity, treat Twins as a pattern ghost: separate interactions, separate sounds, “two locations” feel.
If you can safely compare hunts, note any consistent speed variation between hunts.
If everything stays tightly centred in one room, Twins becomes less likely.
name: The Twins
nightmareTips: Watch for interactions in two places: Twins can interact from a wider combined area, making activity feel “split”.
Hunt speed can vary: one Twin can feel slightly different in speed during hunts.
If you get evidence-like interactions far apart in a short window, keep Twins high.
summary: Split activity can mislead. Track multiple interaction points and timing.

insanityTips: On Insanity, do a controlled electronics test: run a hunt with electronics on vs off and compare speed.
If it feels “powered up” near gear, Raiju is a strong call.
If it’s fast everywhere regardless of electronics, consider Moroi/Jinn/Revenant instead.
name: Raiju
nightmareTips: Electronics speed tell: Raiju gets faster around active electronic equipment during hunts.
If hunts speed up near cameras, DOTS, flashlights, etc., suspect Raiju.
Try turning off/away electronics: if speed drops, Raiju becomes more likely.
summary: Electronics affect its behaviour. Control your equipment placement and use.

insanityTips: On Insanity, UV becomes extra valuable: a single unique handprint can solve the case instantly.
If you observe hunt shapeshift behaviour (brief model changes), Obake becomes very likely.
If UV prints are always normal and there are no shapeshift hints, it may be another ghost.
name: Obake
nightmareTips: UV tell: Obake can leave a unique 6-finger handprint (or unusual UV evidence).
During hunts it can shapeshift briefly (model flicker/shift), which can be a giveaway.
If UV evidence is inconsistent or “odd”, keep Obake in mind.
summary: UV behaviour and prints can help. Confirm with consistent UV checks.

insanityTips: On Insanity, treat Mimic as “inconsistent behaviour”: confirm orbs and then distrust single-trait IDs.
If you’re seeing strong traits from different ghosts in different moments, Mimic is a top candidate.
Use orbs + your one evidence as your anchor, then interpret behaviour second.
name: The Mimic
nightmareTips: Always check for ghost orbs: Mimic can show orbs even though they are not “true” evidence for it.
Behaviour can change (mimicking other ghosts), so don’t lock in too early based on one hunt.
If you have a set of evidence that fits Mimic but the ghost behaves like multiple types, suspect Mimic.
summary: Tricky because it also shows Ghost Orbs. Treat orbs as a clue, not proof.

insanityTips: On Insanity, track sanity and speed: if it feels faster the lower your sanity gets, Moroi is a strong call.
If you get cursed early, the investigation becomes a timer—prioritise tests quickly.
If speed is constant and not sanity-linked, look at other fast ghosts instead.
name: Moroi
nightmareTips: Curse clue: Moroi can “curse” you via Spirit Box/Parabolic, causing faster sanity drain.
Hunt speed increases as your sanity drops; later hunts can feel significantly faster.
If the ghost ramps up speed over time as sanity falls, Moroi becomes likely.
summary: Cursed by voice responses. Manage sanity and watch speed changes over time.

insanityTips: On Insanity, Deogen is one of the safest confirmations if you know what to do: let it approach and listen for the slowdown.
If it cannot be shaken by hiding and always seems to path directly to you, Deogen rises quickly on the list.
If it loses you easily while you hide, it’s probably not Deogen.
name: Deogen
nightmareTips: Hide test: you can’t reliably hide from a Deogen—it will find you even in good hiding spots.
It is very fast when far away, but becomes very slow when it gets close to you.
If a hunt starts terrifying and then becomes easy to loop because it slows near you, suspect Deogen.
summary: Chase behaviour is unique. Test by controlling distance and loop behaviour.

insanityTips: On Insanity, treat Thaye as “front-loaded danger”: early pressure followed by a clear drop in activity.
If hunts become slower/less frequent as time passes (without other explanations), Thaye is likely.
If it ramps up instead of calming down, it’s probably not Thaye.
name: Thaye
nightmareTips: Thaye “ages” during the investigation when players are near it: it starts very aggressive and gets weaker over time.
If early activity/wiki/Hunt are intense and later it calms down noticeably, suspect Thaye.
If you have a Ouija Board, its reported age can increase over time, confirming Thaye.
summary: Changes over time. Early aggressiveness can fade — track it acrosss minutes.

insanityTips: On Insanity, treat Gallu as a “state-cycle” ghost: note whether it gets worse after protective use, then eases later.
If you can control usage, test one protective action and watch for a noticeable behavioural shift.
If behaviour stays consistent regardless of protection, it may be a different ghost.
name: Gallu
nightmareTips: Gallu reacts strongly to protective gear: using items like incense/crucifix interaction can shift its behaviour cycle.
If it feels like it changes state over time (enraged → tired/weakened), keep Gallu in mind.
If “playing safe” early seems to make it scarier before it calms, that pattern fits Gallu.
summary: A newer ghost type. Start with fast EMF/Spirit Box checks and confirm UV evidence reliably.

insanityTips: On Insanity, use a controlled movement test: move near the room, then stop completely and compare response.
If it consistently punishes movement but becomes calmer when you hold still, Dayan becomes very likely.
If movement has no impact on behaviour, it’s probably not Dayan.
name: Dayan
nightmareTips: Movement-based ghost: it gains strength when people move near it and weakens when players stand still nearby.
If activity spikes while you’re walking around the room but calms when you freeze, suspect Dayan.
Treat “stand still” as both a safety tool and an identification test.
summary: A newer ghost type. Use orbs and Spirit Box early, then confirm UV to lock it in.

insanityTips: On Insanity, treat Obambo as “mood swings”: don’t assume consistency—look for alternating calm/aggressive phases.
If you get sudden rapid hunts after a calm stretch, Obambo is a strong candidate.
If behaviour stays steady and predictable, it may be another ghost.
name: Obambo
nightmareTips: Obambo switches between calm and aggressive states, making it feel unpredictable.
If you notice bursts of early hunting/aggression followed by calmer tracking periods, suspect Obambo.
Team play helps: one person watching activity can spot the “mode shift” pattern more clearly.
summary: A newer ghost type. Consistent EMF activity + orbs + UV is your cleanest confirmation path.
